task_family: tabular binary classification under disjoint-group covariate shift (test set is four product codes never seen in train; rank metric)

test_window.evidence: No date/time column anywhere. product_code partitions the data completely: train holds A,B,C,D,E (5100/5250/5765/5112/5343 rows) and test holds F,G,H,I (5422/5107/5018/5228 rows) with ZERO overlap. attribute_0..attribute_3 are constant within each product_code (A=material_7,material_8,9,5 / B=material_5,material_5,8,8 / C=material_7,material_8,5,8 / D=material_7,material_5,6,6 / E=material_7,material_6,6,9 in train; F=material_5,material_6,6,4 / G=material_5,material_6,9,7 / H=material_7,material_7,7,9 / I=material_7,material_5,9,5 in test), so those four columns are aliases of the group key, not independent features — and every test group presents an attribute combination absent from train. id is a contiguous continuation (train 0..26569, test 26570..47344), i.e. the table was split by product block, not shuffled. Per-column null rates match closely across train/test (loading 0.94% vs 1.07%, measurement_17 8.60% vs 8.38%), so the generating process is shared even though the groups are not.
test_window.consequence: The evaluated quantity is generalization to UNSEEN product codes. Any signal that is group-specific is worthless at test time; any validation that lets a model see the held-out group is optimistic.

split_policy.scheme: GroupKFold / leave-one-product-code-out on product_code — exactly 5 groups in train, so 5-fold LOGO is the natural and complete scheme. Each fold trains on 4 codes and scores on the 1 held-out code, mirroring the train->test regime. Report the pooled out-of-fold AUC AND the 5 per-fold AUCs; fold spread is the shift-robustness diagnostic.
forbidden: shuffled KFold or StratifiedKFold that ignores product_code — it leaks group identity into the fold and measures within-group ranking, which is NOT what the leaderboard evaluates

using product_code, attribute_0, attribute_1, attribute_2, attribute_3 as raw model features — they are constant per group, take only 5 values in train, and take 4 UNSEEN values in test; a model that splits on them cannot transfer and will memorize the training groups
target encoding of product_code or of any attribute_* column, for the same reason

fitting any imputer, scaler, or encoder on train+test jointly across groups without re-fitting per group (see data_level ideas — per-group fitting is the intended design, cross-group fitting is the leak)
split_policy.group_key: product_code (5 levels in train, 4 disjoint levels in test)
split_policy.notes: 26,570 train rows over 5 groups: LOGO is cheap. Fold sizes are near-equal (5100-5765) and per-group failure rates are tight (0.2004-0.2273), so folds are naturally balanced without stratification; stratifying inside a group fold is unnecessary and would break the group structure.

metric.name: AUC-ROC
traps: rank-only: absolute calibration and any decision threshold are irrelevant to the score. Do NOT tune a threshold (this repo has confirmed twice — titanic, spaceship-titanic — that CV-tuned thresholds do not transfer), and do not spend effort on probability calibration for its own sake.

the leaderboard AUC is POOLED over all four unseen product codes at once. A model can rank perfectly inside each group and still lose score if its score distribution SHIFTS between groups (group A's non-failures scoring above group B's failures). Per-group score standardization / rank-normalization at inference is therefore a first-class candidate, not a cosmetic step — and it must be validated under LOGO, where the same pathology is visible across the 5 train groups.

21.26% positive rate is mild imbalance and AUC is a rank metric, so resampling / SMOTE / scale_pos_weight buy nothing on the metric and mainly add variance. Class weighting only changes the score monotonically-per-model, which AUC is invariant to.

expected AUC ceiling on this data is low (weak signal, heavy shift): fold-to-fold and seed-to-seed noise will be comparable to real gains. Compare candidates on identical folds and identical seeds, and prefer repeated-seed LOGO before accepting any small win.

compute CV as a single AUC over the pooled out-of-fold prediction vector, and separately as the mean of per-group AUCs — the two disagree exactly when the cross-group scale problem above is present, which makes the gap a useful diagnostic rather than a bookkeeping detail.

external_data.reason: config.yaml special_rules permits external data (external_data_allowed: true, internet_access_allowed: true, pretrained_models_allowed: true), so this is a joinability verdict, not a rules verdict. No whitelisted source has a constructible join key: there is no country, region, currency, date, or entity-name column anywhere in the 26-column schema. product_code (A-I) and attribute_0/1 (material_5..material_8) are opaque synthetic labels with no external referent, so World Bank (country x year), holiday calendars (country x date), ISO tables (country), ECB rates (currency x month) and OWID COVID (country x date) are all unjoinable. The provided measurements are the full covariate set.

data_level: PER-PRODUCT-CODE imputation, fit within each group independently (including each test group on its own). Missingness is substantial and rises monotonically along the measurement index: measurement_3 1.43% -> measurement_17 8.60% in train (1.58% -> 8.38% in test), plus loading ~1%. Because each test group is a fresh population, an imputer fit on train groups and applied to F-I is itself a shift vector; fitting per group is the shift-safe design and is legitimate (test features are fully observable, only the label is not).

Model-based recovery of the high-missing measurements rather than mean/median fill: measurement_17 (8.6% missing) and its high-index neighbours are the most-missing and, given the monotone missingness ladder, likely the most informative. Fit a within-group regression of each high-missing measurement on the low-missing ones (measurement_3..measurement_9, loading) and impute from it; compare against plain per-group median under LOGO before adopting.

Missingness-as-signal features: per-row count of NaNs, and a binary null indicator per measurement column. Missingness rate is near-identical across train and test, so these features are shift-stable — unlike the raw group identity.

Per-group standardization / rank-transform of every continuous feature (loading, measurement_3..17) so that feature scales are comparable across the four unseen codes. This is the direct data-level answer to the pooled-AUC scale trap above.

log or rank transform of `loading` — right-skewed (min 33.16, median 122.39, mean 127.83, max 385.86, std 39.03) and the single named non-measurement continuous column, which makes it the most likely dominant predictor.

DROP product_code and attribute_0..attribute_3 from the feature matrix (they are group aliases with unseen test levels). If any attribute-derived signal is wanted, derive it as a within-group STATISTIC (e.g. group mean/std of loading) rather than as the categorical level itself — but validate under LOGO, since a 5-group sample makes group-level statistics extremely easy to overfit.

Treat measurement_0, measurement_1, measurement_2 as low-cardinality discrete (29/30/25 distinct integer values) rather than continuous — worth a raced lane, but they are stored as int and may simply be coarse counts.

Interaction / aggregate candidates grounded in the schema rather than search: sum and std of measurement_3..17 per row, loading x (row missing-count), and measurement ratios within the correlated high-index block.
model_level: Under disjoint-group shift with a weak-signal rank metric, the bias-dominated end of the model space is the favoured regime: a small, heavily-regularized logistic regression on a handful of transformed features is a serious contender, not a baseline to discard. Race it against GBDT from the start rather than after.

Constrain GBDT capacity hard (shallow depth, high min_child_samples, strong L1/L2, low feature fraction) — deep unregularized trees carve group-specific structure that cannot exist in F-I. Validate every capacity setting under LOGO, never under shuffled CV.

Rank-average rather than probability-average when blending: the metric is rank-based, so averaging per-model ranks is scale-safe across members whose score distributions differ (and it composes with the per-group rank-normalization above).

Feature-count ablation is a first-class experiment here, not tuning trim: with 4-group training and unseen test groups, fewer features often generalizes strictly better. Race an explicit small-feature-set lane.

TASK-BLEND-DECOR is not matched yet — its trigger is observed at blend time. If the pool ends up dominated by deep low-regularization GBDTs, add one shallow heavily-regularized diverse-library member as a decorrelator before re-optimizing weights. Note the prior's NNLS clause is stated for RMSE-family metrics; AUC is not RMSE-family, so use a rank-space weight search (or logit-space NNLS as an approximation) and verify the chosen weights under LOGO rather than assuming the closed form applies.

Adversarial validation (train vs test, features only) is the cheap direct measurement of how large the group shift is and which columns carry it; features that are near-perfect train/test discriminators are shift vectors and are demotion candidates. This is a Stage 1 action seeded here.

prior_match_notes.summary: No [TASK-*] entry in knowledge/task_priors.md fires on this competition. The dominant structural fact here — the test set is a set of DISJOINT GROUPS with unseen categorical levels, which mandates GroupKFold and penalizes capacity — has no corresponding prior. That is a genuine gap in the prior library, not an absence of structure in the problem, and is the strongest write-back candidate for this competition (proposed name: TASK-GROUP-SHIFT, trigger: a categorical key whose train and test level sets are disjoint).
